companies.covenants_and_key_terms: Campus-level SPV high-yield notes (ComputeCo, ComputeCo 2, ComputeCo 3), each secured by first-priority liens on substantially all SPV and guarantor assets. Parent credit support is limited to customary completion guarantees. The 9.25% notes were issued at 97 and the 6.75% at 98, so OID adds to cost. Parent converts are unsecured with conversion permitted from Mar 1, 2030. The CFO says more than 80% of principal matures in fiscal 2031 or later. Indenture covenants (DSCR, distributions) not retrieved.
companies.credit_view: APLD has 1.41 GW of executed 15-year leases (~$36B base-term contracted revenue, ~$86B with renewals) with CoreWeave and a high-IG hyperscaler, but only 250 MW is live. Gross debt is ~$6.4B against DERIVED LTM adjusted EBITDA of ~$171M, inflated by fit-out pass-through revenue, for gross leverage of ~37x. Coupon run-rate (~$486M/yr) is ~3x LTM EBITDA. Credit quality therefore rests on construction delivery and on the ring-fenced SPV structures rather than parent cash flow. The CoreWeave-backed PF1 9.25% paper is the weakest tenant credit; PF2 notes (IG tenant) priced 250bp tighter. The key risk is funding PF3 and Delta Forge 1-2 (~810 MW) while parent liquidity ($2.9B unrestricted) is consumed by equity contributions and capex of ~$2B/quarter.

companies.covenants_and_key_terms: Three ring-fenced, single-asset project SPVs. Each issuer's notes are secured by first-priority liens on substantially all SPV and guarantor assets plus a pledge of issuer equity, with a customary parent completion guarantee. companies.credit_view: CIFR's secured debt is backed by 538 MW of long-term leases: AWS at Black Pearl (300 MW) and Stingray (70 MW), and Fluidstack with a Google backstop at Barber Lake (168 MW). Project debt is ~$8.4M per contracted MW, and the projects are fully funded through restricted cash. Net debt is a modest $1,456M against ~$793M of expected run-rate NOI. Ratings (Ba2-Ba3 / BB-) reflect tenant quality capped by construction and single-asset risk. The parent is weak today: LTM adjusted EBITDA is about -$76M, interest expense runs ~$67M a quarter, and the $1.3B 0% 2031 converts plus 2030 converts depend on HPC rent ramping on schedule. Delivery on Black Pearl's schedule and Barber Lake rent commencement (Oct 2026) are the near-term credit drivers.

companies.subsequent_events: Jul 6, 2026: subsidiary Raylan Data LLC signed a 20-year lease with Anthropic PBC for ~401 MW at Justified Data Campus, Hawesville, KY (~$19B contracted revenue; first capacity 2H 2027, full 2028). Same day: definitive agreement to sell the 50.1% Abernathy JV stake to a Fluidstack-led group for ~$530M (installments above). Jul 9-10, 2026 (Bloomberg): WULF lining up ~$3.5B of debt for Justified Data, a mix of leveraged loans (its first TLB) and high-yield bonds, Morgan Stanley leading; banks in the existing $250M revolver may join. No pricing or closing found as of Oct 9, 2026. Mid-Jul 2026: second CB-3 data hall ready for service. Oct 8, 2026: stock -8%.
companies.covenants_and_key_terms: WULF Compute notes: first-lien project bond with semiannual amortization after initial-phase completion, an excess-cash-flow offer to repurchase, and a parent completion guarantee. Collateral includes the tenant lockbox and Google's warrant pledge. Interest is paid Apr 15 and Oct 15. Parent converts: $1.1B classified current at Jun 30, 2026, likely because conversion triggers were met (equity-settleable). The $100M bridge loan was repaid Apr 16, 2026 after a 54.51M-share equity offering, with a $7.3M extinguishment loss.
companies.credit_view: WULF pairs a Google-supported Fluidstack lease base at Lake Mariner (102 MW live, 336 MW under construction) with a new 401 MW Anthropic lease (~$19B). The Lake Mariner project bond (~$7.3M of debt per Lake Mariner MW, derived) is well supported by tenant and Google credit support. The parent is thin: book equity is only $147.5M, adjusted EBITDA is negative (Q2 -$18.3M), and H1'26 operating cash burn was $154M against $1.38B of H1 capex. $2.5B of converts are structurally subordinated to the SPV, and $1.1B are classified current. Net debt is ~$2.7B (gross $5,725M less $3,029M of cash and restricted cash). The Abernathy exit adds ~$530M of liquidity, but the Justified build needs ~$3.5B of new secured debt not yet placed. Execution and the timing of rent commencement drive the credit.

companies.covenants_and_key_terms: Two investment-grade, fully amortizing 16-year project bonds at bankruptcy-remote SPVs, non-recourse to Hut 8 Corp, secured by first liens and equity pledges, with construction and DSRA escrows. Tenor matches the 15-year leases, which avoids refinancing risk. Beacon Point priced 20bp tighter than River Bend. The parent's only recourse debt is BTC-collateralized lending (FalconX $200M at 7%, Apr 2027). Total principal payments in H1'26 were $217.7M.
companies.credit_view: HUT has the strongest structure of the four. Its $7.5B of debt sits in two investment-grade (BBB-/Baa2), fully amortizing project bonds matched to 15-year triple-net leases: Fluidstack with a Google backstop at River Bend, and an AA- or better tenant at Beacon Point. Construction is pre-funded with $6.8B of restricted cash. Project debt is ~$12.6M per financed MW (597 MW), the highest of the group, consistent with turnkey IG builds at tight spreads. The parent is light: $234M unrestricted cash, minimal EBITDA ($10.4M Q2 ex-MTM), and liquidity reliant on BTC holdings and the ABTC stake. Phase 2 at Beacon Point needs a further multi-billion financing. Ratings stay project-level; any parent rating would be constrained by negative operating cash flow and BTC volatility.
